\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تقصیر} (taqsir)}{تقصیر (taqsir)}]{\fa{تقصیر} (taqsir) — a fault, the blame}

\label{lesson:FA-C376-taqsir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be worth it, then the Persian for to pay off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تقصیر}}
\textbf{\fa{تقصیر}} (\emph{taqsir}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fault, the blame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{تقصیر} \fa{من} \fa{نبود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in taqsir-e man nabud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It wasn't my fault.
\end{quote}

\emph{Taqsir-e kasi budan} — to be someone's fault. Very common in speech.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تقصیر}} comes from Arabic \emph{taqṣīr} (EtymDB), a verbal noun usually explained as falling short; in Persian it is the fault or the blame.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taqsir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{taqsir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be worth it, then the Persian for to pay off, then say \emph{taqsir} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گناه} (gonâh)}{گناه (gonâh)}]{\fa{گناه} (gonâh) — a sin; guilt}

\label{lesson:FA-C376-gonah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to pay off, then the Persian for a fault.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گناه}}
\textbf{\fa{گناه}} (\emph{gonâh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a sin; guilt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دزدی} \fa{گناه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dozdi gonâh ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Stealing is a sin.
\end{quote}

\emph{Gonâh-e u nist} — it is not his fault. \emph{Gonâhkâr} — guilty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{گناه}} is an inherited Persian word, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{wināh} \textquotedblleft{}sin, offence\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نقطه} \fa{ضعف} (noqte-ye za'f)}{نقطه ضعف (noqte-ye za'f)}]{\fa{نقطه} \fa{ضعف} (noqte-ye za'f) — a weak point, a weakness}

\label{lesson:FA-C376-noqte-ye-zaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fault, then the Persian for a sin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نقطه} \fa{ضعف}}
\textbf{\fa{نقطه} \fa{ضعف}} (\emph{noqte-ye za'f}) — \textquotedblleft{}a weak point, a weakness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نقطه} \fa{ضعف} \fa{او} \fa{بیصبری} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{noqte-ye za'f-e u bisabri ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His weak point is impatience.
\end{quote}

\emph{Noqte} \textquotedblleft{}point\textquotedblright{} + \emph{za'f} \textquotedblleft{}weakness\textquotedblright{}. The opposite is \emph{noqte-ye qovvat}, a strong point.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{نقطه} \fa{ضعف}} joins two words of Arabic origin with a Persian ezafe: \emph{noqte} from Arabic \emph{nuqṭa} \textquotedblleft{}dot\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), and \emph{za'f}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḍa'f} \textquotedblleft{}weakness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{noqte-ye za'f}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{noqte-ye za'f}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a fault, then the Persian for a sin, then say \emph{noqte-ye za'f} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رخ} \fa{دادن} (rokh dâdan)}{رخ دادن (rokh dâdan)}]{\fa{رخ} \fa{دادن} (rokh dâdan) — to happen, to occur}

\label{lesson:FA-C376-rokh-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a sin, then the Persian for a weak point.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رخ} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{رخ} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{rokh dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to happen, to occur\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{حادثه} \fa{دیشب} \fa{رخ} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in hâdese dishab rokh dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This accident happened last night.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{ettefâq oftâdan}. Stem \emph{rokh deh-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{رخ} \fa{دادن}} \textquotedblleft{}to occur\textquotedblright{} is in EtymDB; it is native Persian, built from \emph{rokh} \textquotedblleft{}face, appearance\textquotedblright{} and \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to PIE \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}: an event shows its face.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اعتراف} \fa{کردن} (e'terâf kardan)}{اعتراف کردن (e'terâf kardan)}]{\fa{اعتراف} \fa{کردن} (e'terâf kardan) — to admit, to confess}

\label{lesson:FA-C376-eteraf-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a weak point, then the Persian for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اعتراف} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{اعتراف} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{e'terâf kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to admit, to confess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{به} \fa{اشتباهش} \fa{اعتراف} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u be eshtebâhash e'terâf kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He admitted his mistake.
\end{quote}

Takes \emph{be}: \emph{be chizi e'terâf kardan}. \emph{E'terâf} \textquotedblleft{}confession\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اعتراف}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{i'tirāf} \textquotedblleft{}confession, admission\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); with \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} it becomes a Persian compound verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
